evidence.note: claim: current ci.yml/Dockerfile float (unpinned --with, no --locked, || echo, tag actions, no digest). Ran pytest tests/test_ci_pinning.py on unfixed tree: 6 failed; after pinning: 6 passed.
ran ddflow brief --item MT-ci-self-pin; rules digest read; no knob involved (pure CI pin), test added

chunk_findings.detail: The new blocking pip-audit step builds its requirements file with `uv export --locked --no-hashes --no-emit-project` but does not exclude development dependencies. `uv export` includes the default development group unless `--no-dev` or an explicit group filter is used, so the audited set is not the “locked runtime set” promised by the step comment. Given a dev-only dependency such as `pytest` (or another CI-only tool) with a known advisory, `pip-audit --strict` will exit non-zero and fail the quality job even though no shipped runtime package is affected; before this change that same advisory was only a warning because of the removed `|| echo`.
chunk_findings.title: .github/workflows/ci.yml:99

chunk_findings.detail:
`test_pip_audit_is_blocking` only requires the substring `pip-audit` to appear in some non-comment line, so a YAML key satisfies it. A ci.yml step such as:
```yaml
- name: pip-audit
  run: echo "no audit"
```
has a code line `- name: pip-audit`, produces no `|| echo` / `|| true` finding, and then passes the final `assert any("pip-audit" in text ...)`. The test therefore can pass even though no `pip-audit` command is executed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:63

chunk_findings.detail:
The advisory check only inspects a fixed four-code-line window starting at the first line containing `pip-audit`, not the full shell command. For a multi-line invocation like:
```yaml
run: |
  pip-audit \
    --strict \
    --desc \
    --fix \
    --dry-run \
    --output report.json \
    || echo "advisory"
```
the window starting at the `pip-audit \` line stops before `|| echo`, so the test passes even though the audit is advisory.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:59

chunk_findings.detail:
`test_dockerfile_base_images_carry_a_digest` treats every `FROM` target as an external image and flags internal build-stage references. A valid multi-stage Dockerfile such as:
```dockerfile
FROM python:3.13-alpine@sha256:... AS builder
FROM builder AS final
```
fails on the second line because `FROM builder` has no `@sha256:` digest, even though `builder` is a prior stage, not a floating base image.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:78

chunk_findings.detail: `test_lock_file_is_checked_for_drift` searches the raw file text, so the assertion is satisfied by comments or step names containing the command. For example, a ci.yml containing only `# uv lock --check` passes even though no drift-check command is run. The test should use `_code_lines` or a command parser rather than `CI.read_text()`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: The `--with` version check only tests that the captured requirement contains the substring `==`. Input such as `uv run --locked --with bandit==` or `uv run --locked --with bandit==*` passes the test even though no exact version is pinned, contrary to the test’s stated “exact version” contract.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:36

chunk_findings.detail:
`test_pip_audit_is_blocking` uses a sliding window of 4 consecutive code lines to check for `|| echo` or `|| true` after `pip-audit`. In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the dependency audit step spans multiple lines:
```yaml
          uv export --locked --no-hashes --no-emit-project > "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements.txt"
          uv run --no-project --with pip-audit==2.10.1 pip-audit --strict --progress-spinner off -r "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements.txt"
          uv run --no-project python scripts/ci/deps-allowlist.py
```
If an error suppression like `|| true` were placed on the `uv export` line or the `deps-allowlist.py` line within the same multi-line run block or step, or if future lines are added between `pip-audit` and an error suppression within a 4-line window, the test fails to inspect the actual execution context correctly or can miss failure-masking operators due to arbitrary line-window slicing. Furthermore, `_code_lines` flattens the file, stripping comments and blank lines, but `lines[i : i + 4]` slices over the filtered code lines rather than logical YAML command blocks, making the window dependent on intervening non-comment lines rather than command boundaries.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_pinning.py:59
